Build estimates and proposals, track budgets, and make sure the studio is paid properly for its time, including when scope grows. Run delivery. Plan timelines, assign tasks and deadlines to everyone (founders included), build in time for reviews, and keep projects moving on very tight schedules. Build the operating system. Set up the processes, tools and rituals the studio runs on. Lean, AI-friendly and with as few meetings as possible. Find, staff and manage teams. Assemble and manage project teams of freelancers, contractors and partners (designers, developers, Shopify, social, production) for each project. Handle two client rhythms. Some clients work fast and almost entirely on Slack; others follow a plan, present and approve cycle for strategy, websites, TikTok Shop and social campaigns. First 30 days: take over day-to-day operations on one client account, learn how the studio works and map current projects, budgets and deadlines. Days 30 to 60: put a simple operating system in place (task assignment, timelines, review cycles, budget tracking) and start leading client communication. Days 60 to 90: own the client relationships across accounts, staff new projects with the right partners, and free the founders to focus on client strategy, big pitches and new business. Must-haves 5 to 8 years of experience in account management, project management or operations at a creative, branding, marketing or digital agency. Nice-to-haves Experience with consumer goods (CPG) brands, especially retail launches at Target, Walmart or similar: packaging updates, product photography, in-store activations and launch timelines. Experience at a small studio or startup, where you built processes from scratch. Who will thrive here You get it fast. You understand the business and the clients in weeks, not months. You're comfortable telling the founders what to do, when, and why, and pushing back respectfully when you see a better way. Clients love working with you. You're warm and trustworthy, and firm on budget and scope when you need to be. You value time. Yours, the team's and the founders'. You protect the studio's margins and make sure its work is valued. This role is not a fit if you: Rely on rigid, old-school processes and many meetings to get things done. Are slow to adopt new tools, technology or AI. You’ve taken over day-to-day operations on active accounts, put simple systems in place for task assignment, timelines, reviews, and budget tracking, and are leading client communication with confidence. The founders are spending less time on project management and more time on strategy, pitches, and growth because delivery is organized, clear, and moving on time. You’ve been the main client contact, handled expectations and scope conversations with confidence, and worked closely on estimates and budgets. You’re comfortable managing multiple stakeholders and external partners at once, and you can create structure quickly in a lean, fast-moving environment. Strong English, modern tools, and a calm, authoritative style are essential, along with the judgment to protect timelines, margins, and client trust.

review_candidates.title: Workforce Business Partner (South South)
review_candidates.description: Who We Are Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month. As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually. Job Title: Workforce Business Partner (South South) Reports to: Team Lead, Workforce Partner Job Purpose The Workforce Business Partner (WBP) serves as a strategic partner to business leaders, driving the alignment of people strategy with business priorities. This role exists to ensure that every people-related initiative — from performance enablement and workforce planning to leadership effectiveness — is executed with precision, empathy, and measurable impact. Beyond traditional HR delivery, the WBP acts as a trusted advisor, shaping organizational health and fostering a culture of accountability, engagement, and inclusion. The role bridges the gap between business needs and people solutions, ensuring that talent is positioned as a key enabler of growth and innovation. Key Responsibilities Partner with business leaders to translate organizational goals into actionable people plans that drive capability, performance, and retention. Lead workforce planning and organizational design discussions to ensure the right structure, roles, and talent are in place to meet current and future needs. Coach and influence leaders on talent strategy, performance management, and Independent Contractor engagement to strengthen leadership effectiveness and team culture. Act as a trusted advisor on IC relations matters, ensuring fair, consistent, and business-aligned resolutions in collaboration with the Workforce Relations COE. Analyze people data and insights to identify trends, risks, and opportunities, presenting data-driven recommendations to business leaders. Champion change management and communication strategies that support transformation, adoption, and continuous improvement within business units. Ensure compliance with internal policies and local labor laws while promoting a positive, high-performance culture. Qualifications 2–4 years of progressive HR experience, including at least 2 years in a Business Partnership or advisory capacity. Demonstrated experience working in fast-paced, matrixed, or multinational environments. Strong understanding of core HR functions — performance management, people relations, organizational design, and workforce planning. Proven ability to use HR data and analytics to inform decision-making. Preferred Qualifications Experience supporting technical or commercial business units in a fintech, banking, or tech environment. Demonstrated success influencing senior stakeholders and leading complex change initiatives. About You You’re a strategic thinker who sees the big picture but executes with precision. You build trust quickly and communicate with empathy, clarity, and confidence. You thrive in ambiguity and can balance multiple stakeholders with ease. You’re data-driven — you make decisions grounded in insight, not intuition. You’re committed to continuous improvement, always seeking better ways to drive business impact through people. What Success Looks Like You have established yourself as a trusted advisor to senior business leaders, influencing key people and organizational decisions. Business units under your support demonstrate improved engagement, retention, and performance outcomes. You’ve delivered a measurable improvement in workforce planning accuracy and performance management effectiveness. Leaders actively seek your input on strategic and people-related matters, not just HR processes. You’ve successfully embedded at least one COE-led initiative (e.g., new policy, performance framework, or workforce process) within your business unit with strong adoption and feedback. Why join us Competitive compensation, comprehensive benefits, and impactful career growth opportunities. Fully remote/flexible work culture backed by continuous support for your learning and professional development.
